newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hainan Airlines prices B share IPO at 3.5-4 yuan.
newsitem.headline: Hainan Airlines prices B share IPO at 3.5-4 yuan.

text.p: Hainan Airlines Co has tentatively priced its initial public offering (IPO) of 71 million B shares at between 3.5 and four yuan, a company official said on Monday.
The firm aims to launch the IPO of foreign currency B shares, to be listed in Shanghai, by the end of May 1997, the official told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
The issue requires the final approval of the China Securities Regulatory Commission, he said.
The company, based in Haikou, capital of Hainan province, has appointed Shenzhen J&A Securities Co as the domestic lead underwriter, the official said.
SocGen-Crosby Securities (HK) Ltd and Indosuez W.I. Carr Securities Ltd are the international coordinators, he added.

Hainan Airlines, which operates 13 planes -- including nine Boeing 737 aircraft -- in mainland China, plans to use the proceeds to expand its main operations, the official said. He declined to elaborate.

Hainan Airlines, which became a shareholding company in 1993, now has 400 million outstanding shares -- 100 million held by American Aviation Investment, 240 million held by domestic institutions and 60 million shares held by individuals.
American Aviation Investment is a fund partially controlled by U.S. financier George Soros, making Hainan Airlines the first Chinese airline to be partly foreign owned.

A Chinese company with six million institutional shares in Hainan Airlines began to auction the shares last Friday in what the Shenzhen-based Securities Times on Monday said was the first share auction case in modern Chinese history.
The Chinese company was ordered by the courts to sell the shares to repay a creditor, the Hainan Airlines official said, but declined to identify the firm.
Of the six million shares, 3.8 million shares have been sold so far to seven bidders for 1.28 yuan per share, compared with an issue price of one yuan in early 1993, the official said.
Hainan Airlines, which operates more than 20 domestic routes, plans to open up links with Hong Kong and other overseas destinations, the official said. He did not give a timetable for the plan.
The company had net earnings of about 81 million yuan in 1995, 87 million yuan in 1994 and 67 million yuan in 1993, he said, but did not provide a figure for 1996.
The company also plans to issue domestic currency A shares after the B share listing, the official said.
